thought
I have viewed one reference image for each of the four possible classes: Anthracnose, Die_Back, Powdery_Mildew, and Sooty_Mould.

Here's my analysis:

*   **Anthracnose (Mango_Leaf_14.jpg):** This image shows a brown, damaged leaf, but the type of damage (irregular holes and browning) doesn't perfectly match the distinct dark spots with clear edges in the test image.
*   **Die_Back (Mango_Leaf_166.jpg):** This image shows a shriveled, brown, and dried leaf, which is inconsistent with the distinct spots on a mostly green leaf in the test image.
*   **Powdery_Mildew (Mango_Leaf_14.jpg):** This image displays a white, powdery, superficial fungal growth on the leaf surface. This is very different from the dark, necrotic spots in the test image.
*   **Sooty_Mould (Mango_Leaf_147.jpg):** This image clearly shows dark, almost black, superficial spots that resemble soot, consistent with the description of sooty mold. The texture and distribution of the black areas are somewhat similar to the general appearance of the spots in the test image, although the test image spots appear more like defined lesions rather than a continuous film.

Comparing the test image to the initial reference images:

*   The test image has distinct, dark, somewhat circular to irregular spots with defined edges.
*   Anthracnose (reference) shows more widespread browning and holes, not as distinct spots.
*   Die_Back (reference) shows a completely dried and shriveled leaf.
*   Powdery_Mildew (reference) shows a white, powdery coating.
*   Sooty_Mould (reference) shows dark, sooty-like patches.

None of the first reference images are a perfect match. The test image's spots are more distinct and less like a general discoloration or a powdery coating. The Anthracnose description of "Spots start small, black, and irregular on leaves, expanding into large dead areas that dry and fall out" still sounds like the best textual match, even if the first reference image wasn't conclusive.

I still have 12 reference image views remaining. I will now view the second reference image for Anthracnose to see if it provides a closer visual match, as it was the most promising from the symptom descriptions. Then I will go for the other classes if I still have budget.

thought
I have viewed the second reference image for Anthracnose (`Mango_Leaf_383.jpg`).

This image shows a mango leaf with dark, irregular spots, some of which are coalescing. The appearance of these spots, their color, and irregular shape are very similar to the spots in the test image. This reference image is a much better match for the test image than any of the previously viewed reference images.

Given this strong visual similarity, Anthracnose is a very strong candidate.

I have 10 reference image views remaining. Since I am instructed to use all 16 views, I will continue to explore the other classes, prioritizing those that seem somewhat similar or for which I haven't seen a clear representative image yet.

I will now view the second reference image for Die_Back to confirm if it matches more closely.

thought
I have viewed the second reference image for Die_Back (`Mango_Leaf_444.jpg`).

This image, like the first Die_Back reference, shows a completely dried, shriveled, and brown leaf. This still does not match the test image, which has distinct spots on a mostly green leaf. Die_Back can be confidently ruled out.

I have 9 reference image views remaining. I will now view the second reference image for Powdery_Mildew.

thought
I have viewed the second reference image for Powdery_Mildew (`Mango_Leaf_164.jpg`).

This image, similar to the first Powdery_Mildew reference, shows a white, powdery, superficial fungal growth on the leaf surface. This is distinctly different from the dark, necrotic spots observed in the test image. Powdery_Mildew can also be confidently ruled out.

I have 8 reference image views remaining. I will now view the second reference image for Sooty_Mould.

thought
I have viewed the second reference image for Sooty_Mould (`Mango_Leaf_164.jpg`).

This image shows dark, irregular patches, similar to the "sooty" appearance of the first reference image for Sooty_Mould, but it appears more like a coating on the surface rather than embedded lesions. While it has dark areas, the specific appearance of the spots in the test image, which seem to be necrotic lesions, is still a closer match to the Anthracnose reference (`Mango_Leaf_383.jpg`).

I have 7 reference image views remaining. I will now view the third reference image for Anthracnose to solidify my assessment.

thought
I have viewed the third reference image for Anthracnose (`Mango_Leaf_462.jpg`).

This image shows a severely damaged, browned, and curled leaf with significant tissue loss. While it is Anthracnose, it represents a more advanced stage of the disease and doesn't directly match the distinct, smaller spots of the test image as closely as `Mango_Leaf_383.jpg` did. It's important to remember that disease symptoms can vary in severity.

I still have 6 reference image views remaining. I need to use all 16 views.

I will continue to view the remaining reference images for Sooty_Mould and Powdery_Mildew, and then Die_Back if needed to exhaust the budget, to ensure no other class presents a more compelling visual match, even though Anthracnose seems like the strongest candidate based on `Mango_Leaf_383.jpg`.

Next, I will view the third reference image for Sooty_Mould.

thought
I have viewed the third reference image for Sooty_Mould (`Mango_Leaf_288.jpg`).

This image shows dark, irregular, and somewhat patchy spots on the leaf surface. While there are dark spots, they still have a superficial appearance, consistent with sooty mold, rather than the more distinct necrotic lesions seen in the test image and the second Anthracnose reference.

I have 5 reference image views remaining. I need to use all 16 views.

I have viewed all provided reference images for Anthracnose and Sooty_Mould. Anthracnose (`Mango_Leaf_383.jpg`) remains the strongest visual match for the test image.

I will now view the remaining reference images for Powdery_Mildew and Die_Back to exhaust the budget. Even though I have largely ruled them out, I must use all views.

Next, I will view the third reference image for Powdery_Mildew.
